overview: Zimbabwe's women's health innovation ecosystem is small but active, anchored by maternal and reproductive health where the burden is heaviest. Local ventures like Tariro Health (MamaBot AI) and Afrimom pair AI and mobile channels with Shona, Ndebele and English content to reach underserved mothers, while the government has digitised maternal death surveillance and funded free sanitary products for schoolgirls. Cervical cancer, the leading cancer among Zimbabwean women, is drawing HPV testing scale-up and AI screening pilots. Dedicated local femtech capital is thin, so most funding flows through government commitments, global grant programs and regional gender-lens funds.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent momentum centres on AI maternal tools, cervical cancer screening and menstrual health.

items.text: National statistics show Zimbabwe's maternal mortality ratio declining, with 563 maternal deaths recorded across 410,051 deliveries in 2025.
Tariro Health's MamaBot AI offers 24/7 pregnancy, newborn and mental health guidance free via web, WhatsApp and SMS in English, Shona and Ndebele.
Over 30,000 HPV DNA cervical cancer tests conducted in Mashonaland West Province, with an AI screening tool set for field validation in Zimbabwe.
Zimbabwe's 2025 budget allocates ZiG85 million (about USD 3.27 million) for free sanitary products for schoolgirls to reduce period poverty.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Government policy pairs digital health surveillance with financing commitments for family planning and menstrual health.

items.text: Zimbabwe revitalised and rolled out the Electronic Maternal and Perinatal Death Notification System (eMPDNS), co-designed with frontline workers, lifting reporting from 10% to 40%.
At the International Conference on Family Planning, Zimbabwe pledged an additional USD 2.25 million yearly for contraceptive procurement in 2026 and 2027.
National Family Planning Strategy 2022-2026 targets universal, affordable contraceptive access via community-based distribution and integration with HIV and maternal health services.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Local ventures and hubs are building AI and mobile tools for maternal and reproductive health.

items.text: Tariro Health positions itself as Zimbabwe's maternal health innovation hub, combining MamaBot AI, immunisation tracking and affordable smart birth kits for clinics across Harare and rural areas.
Afrimom, built by Fintum Health, runs a virtual women's clinic over SMS and mobile app, connecting pregnant women to obstetricians, clinics and reproductive health support in local languages.
Vaxiglobal deploys AI and facial biometrics to verify vaccine delivery, reaching 210,000 women in Mashonaland Central and staffing a team that is 62% women.
Rural youth and school-based initiatives (e.g. Tsiga Primary School, Mutoko) sew reusable menstrual pads to keep girls in school, backed by UNICEF, CAMFED, CARE and DAPP.
